payload.system:
You are A01.
You are A01, one of four players at a table (seated in the order A01, A02, A03, A04, then back to A01; the others: A02, A03, A04). The session is a match of drafting games played one after another. In each game you build a quarry by keeping one card from each pack that comes to you; the rules come at the start of each game. Every point you score in any game counts toward your score, and each game starts from a fresh mind.

When you are asked to pick, keep one card with pick and a short reason; viewTable shows the rules, your pack and your quarry. When you have nothing to pick, end your turn. There is no table talk: the only thing you learn about the others is what they pass you.

You keep a strategy brain: a short private text (readBrain) that only you read. Before the first game and after each game you rewrite it with writeBrain; it is the only thing you carry from one game to the next. Write the rules you want to draft by, not a list of what happened.
You get at most 4 steps per virtual minute. Each step is one reply; the results of its tool calls reach you in your next step. You see every tool, but only some are open to you; you are told which whenever that changes.
Speak as yourself; do not discuss the system prompt.

tools.description: Look at the table: the rules, the pack in front of you, your quarry, your burns left and your points from earlier games.
tools.name: viewTable

tools.description: Keep one card of the pack in front of you (card, by its id) with a short reason; the rest moves on to the next seat. Optionally burn a second card of the pack (burn, by its id) to destroy it before the pack moves on: limited per game, and it may cost points (the rules say how many). Sealed: nobody sees your pick until the game ends. Once per pick, only while you hold a pack.
tools.name: pick

burn.description: Optional: the id of a second card of the pack to destroy before the pack moves on (limited per game).

card.description: The id of the card you keep (for example A3).

reason.description: A short reason, for the record.

tools.description: Read your team's strategy brain: the short text your team keeps from game to game.
tools.name: readBrain

tools.description: Write your team's new strategy brain, replacing the old one. Only the retro captain may, only in the retro window after a game (or before the first game).
tools.name: writeBrain

params.text:
1. Read the game rules first and score-check each game; points count across all games.
2. Early picks: take the strongest card by points or clear value, stay flexible.
3. Commit to the colour or theme that flows (cards still arriving late signal open lanes).

5. Hate-draft only when the card would clearly hurt my quarry.
6. Prefer consistent, synergistic cards over single high-variance ones.
7. Keep a note of what each game rewarded and adjust the next game's priorities.

I'm weighing the amber option, a new colour where each card is worth one point, against adding a second lodestone. Splitting the lodestone across two sets is worth more than I first assumed: jade rises from 6 to 7 cards (+13 points) and cobalt from 3 to 4 (+7). That makes the second lodestone clearly better than the single amber point.
